item.title: Mike and Jay Talk About It Ends
item.author: RedLetterMedia
item.content:encoded: Mike and Jay both enjoyed a little film called "It Ends" and wanted to have a chat about it. Often cited as having a misleading ad campaign making the film look more like a horror movie about zombies trying to get you as you drive down a road in a car, the movie is more a laid back existential thriller about the most terrifying thing of all - having to be alive with your own nasty ass. Dealing with the shock that once you leave college and head out into the real world, that life is nothing but an endless series of holidays, routines, chores and then you die.

item.title: MOTHER MARY - with David Lowery
item.content:encoded: SEASON 2 - EPISODE 212 MOTHER MARY - with David LoweryIn this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, director David Lowery (Season 2, Episode 60) returns to discuss his latest film, MOTHER MARY, now available to stream at home. Throughout the episode, we discuss the making of the movie, and topics include: the origin of the two lead characters, shooting the dialogue-heavy script, the evolution of the concert footage, and filming the bulk of the movie in 2023 and the remainder in 2024. We learn how the "ghost" was visualized and captured practically, where the supernatural elements of the movie came from, how actress Anne Hathaway prepared for her character's elaborate dance choreography, and why the film was shot in Germany even though it's set in England. David also shares how the process of developing MOTHER MARY differed and mirrored the development of his other films. In addition to learning how David filmed the movie, we also discuss how much work was done in post, and David reveals the level of invisible VFX work in the final cut. Plus, David shares some information about his next project.Recommended Viewing: MOTHER MARYThis episode is sponsored by Aputure

item.title: EDDIE MARSAN - Actor
item.content:encoded: SEASON 2 - EPISODE 211 Eddie Marsan - ActorIn this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with actor Eddie Marsan (NO ORDINARY HEIST, BACK TO BLACK, RAY DONOVAN). During our conversation, we discuss Eddie's youth in East London, being discovered by casting in a club at 18, his disciplined approach to his craft, working with a range of directors including Mike Leigh (Season 1, Episode 76), Edgar Wright (Season 2, Episode 169), and Steven Spielberg, playing a countless number of supporting roles, and the shortcomings of filmmakers who fail to give working and lower class characters volition, autonomy, and humanity. Eddie also reflects on acting as "evil" characters, and we discuss the qualities of several of them from throughout his career. Towards the end of the episode, we ask Eddie how younger generations of actors are different compared to the ones who came before, and he encourages young actors to not wait for the system to change and create space for the roles they want to play. Plus, Eddie reveals the type of character he'd love to play but has yet to.This episode is sponsored by Aputure

item.title: When an Actor’s Career Fell Apart – Wesley Snipes
item.author: FilmStack
item.content:encoded:
By the late 90s, Wesley Snipes was everywhere.
He broke through with New Jack City, proved he could carry a comedy with White Men Can’t Jump, became an action star with Passenger 57 and Demolition Man, and still found time for films like To Wong Foo and One Night Stand, where he won Best Actor at the Venice Film Festival.
But in 1998, he became Blade.
Blade became the defining role of Snipes’ career. But as Blade got bigger, the rest of his career started slowing down.
Within a few years, the major studio roles were disappearing, stories about his on-set antics were spreading, and legal trouble was about to take him away for years.
This is the story of when an actor disappeared from Hollywood, and how he had to skate uphill to find his way back. This is Wesley Snipes.

item.title: The Decade Hollywood Stopped Saying No
item.author: FilmStack
item.content:encoded:
When Hollywood felt the pressure, they panicked. And what did they do? They gave a generation of directors more control than ever before. That decision sent shockwaves through the film industry and resulted in one of the biggest transformative periods in Hollywood. This was the 1970s and we are still living with the effects from this time period.
Some of the biggest directors ever shined during this time. Steven Spielberg, George Lucas, Francis Ford Coppola, Robert Altman, Martin Scorsese, and more. These directors evolved the film industry more than any others. From Jaws to Star Wars to Apocalypse Now to The Exorcist, this video covers the 1970s like no other video.
This is a story of when Hollywood lost it's way, then lost control, then took that control back, all because of the same reasons.

item.title: RON HOWARD - Director
item.content:encoded: SEASON 2 - EPISODE 210 Ron Howard - DirectorIn this episode of the Team Deakins Podcast, we speak with director Ron Howard (AVEDON, APOLLO 13, A BEAUTIFUL MIND). Ron has worked professionally in film and television since the age of 4, and he reflects on his life and career throughout the episode, from chewing fake glass with Yul Brenner as a child actor to directing a wide variety of features and documentaries for almost 50 years. A graduate of the Roger Corman movie factory, Ron reveals what he learned about leadership and collaboration while directing GRAND THEFT AUTO, his directorial debut, under Roger's guidance, and we discuss whether any modern equivalent exists for filmmakers today as a proving ground. Ron also shares how he pushed himself early on to always be creating, and we discuss the creation of several of his films and what he aims for in every movie he makes. We later ask what draws him to a potential project, and we discuss his foray into directing documentaries and how it differs from shooting fiction. We worked with Ron on A BEAUTIFUL MIND, and we had a wonderful time catching up with him.This episode is sponsored by Aputure ⁠
